thread:
nina: Heads-up — onboarding aurora-v2 embeddings for search. Quick QA shows recall@50 down ~4% vs master on short queries. Can someone triage? Dashboard: https://redwood-evals/aurora-v2 (internal)
alex: On it. Which quant/config did you use for the failing run? per-tensor int8 or per-channel?

nina: We ran per-tensor int8 via ONNX static quant (calib on heldout). Baseline fp32 numbers + int8 pasted below.
```
Model               recall@1  recall@10  recall@50  silhouette_mean
aurora-v2-fp32       0.412     0.678      0.812       0.21
aurora-v2-int8       0.405     0.660      0.771       0.14
baseline-bert        0.398     0.645      0.742       0.16
```

maria: silhouette drop is interesting — suggests clusters compressed. Did you check embedding norms / cosine distribution shift? :thinking_face:

nina: Yep — mean L2 norm down ~8% after quant. Also UMAP shows trajectory contraction for long-tail docs. Quick norm check script we used: 
```python
# quick norm check
import numpy as np
vecs_fp32 = np.load('fp32_val.npy')
vecs_int8 = np.load('int8_val.npy')
print(vecs_fp32.mean(axis=0).mean(), vecs_int8.mean(axis=0).mean())
```

sam: Any pooling/tokenization changes between the checkpoints? Aurora-v2 had a recent change to CLS-mean hybrid pooling, could matter for short queries.

nina: We used mean pooling in this run. Re-running with CLS pooling to compare now.

dev-bot: perf-runner started job j-7781 for aurora-v2-pooler-compare, ETA ~12m

alex: If pooling swap doesn't resolve it, try per-channel quantization or symmetric vs asymmetric quant. Per-channel tends to preserve directional components better. I can spin per-channel on staging.

nina: Good idea. Also stratified the recall delta by query length — short queries lost most of the signal.

cheng: Quick plot I made: recall_delta_vs_len.png shows ~-6% for qlen<=3, ~0% for qlen>12. Looks concentrated at the head.

maria: Could this be due to prefix tokens / special tokens being handled differently? Any change in tokenizer or truncation?

nina: No truncation/tokenizer differences. Hypothesis: quantization interacting with the projection layer (128->512) — small bias shifts get amplified for short inputs, since they rely on fewer context tokens.

sam: We can try a tiny affine calibration per-dim on the heldout: compute scale/bias to match fp32 means and apply before normalization. Low-risk and cheap.

nina: That sounds promising. Alex — can you run per-channel int8 + affine calib on the heldout and report recall@50? If improvement >2% we can promote to canary.

alex: ACK. Kicking off per-channel+calib job now, will report in ~25m. @ops-bot can you ensure staging has capacity?

ops-bot: staging-autoscaler: +4 GPUs allocated to eng-ml-staging for aurora tests (request j-7782).

nina: Thanks everyone — I'll update the eval dashboard with the UMAP snapshots and open a tiny PR with the norm-check and affine scripts. Will follow up after alex's run. :thumbsup:
